description:
Signed-off-by: NAYANA.R <nayana.r7813@gmail.com>

closes #3644 

## 💡 Fix Description

This fix ensures that the visibility query parameter is correctly applied when listing tools using admin tokens.

Previously, admin tokens bypassed access control in a way that caused the visibility filter (public, team, private) to be ignored. As a result, requests like /tools?visibility=team or /tools?visibility=private returned the full list of tools instead of only the tools matching the specified visibility.

The fix ensures that the explicit visibility filter provided in the request is always honored, even when using an admin token. Admin bypass now only affects access permissions, not the filtering logic.

Testing confirmed that:

/tools?visibility=public returns only public tools

/tools?visibility=team returns only team tools

/tools?visibility=private returns only private tools

This restores consistent behavior between admin and non-admin tokens when applying visibility filters.

Testing 


1. Create PRIVATE tools

for i in {1..5}; do
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4444/tools \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCPGATEWAY_BEARER_TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "{
      \"tool\": {
        \"name\": \"private-tool-$i\",
        \"description\": \"Private test tool $i\",
        \"visibility\": \"private\"
      }
    }"
done


Verify PRIVATE filter
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCPGATEWAY_BEARER_TOKEN_ADMIN" \
"http://localhost:4444/tools?visibility=private&limit=0" | jq '. | length'

2.Create TEAM tools

for i in {1..5}; do
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4444/tools \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCPGATEWAY_BEARER_TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "{
      \"tool\": {
        \"name\": \"team-tool-$i\",
        \"description\": \"Team test tool $i\",
        \"visibility\": \"team\",
        \"teamId\": \"team-1\"
      }
    }"
done

Verify TEAM filter

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCPGATEWAY_BEARER_TOKEN_ADMIN" \
"http://localhost:4444/tools?visibility=team&limit=0" | jq '. | length'

3. Create PUBLIC tools
for i in {1..5}; do
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4444/tools \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCPGATEWAY_BEARER_TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "{
      \"tool\": {
        \"name\": \"public-tool-$i\",
        \"description\": \"Public test tool $i\",
        \"visibility\": \"public\"
      }
    }"
done

Verify PUBLIC filter
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCPGATEWAY_BEARER_TOKEN_ADMIN" \
"http://localhost:4444/tools?visibility=public&limit=0" | jq '. | length'
 


## 🧪 Verification

|---------------------------------------|----------------------|--------|
| Lint suite                            | `make lint`          |Pass    |
| Unit tests                            | `make test`          |Pass    |

reviews.body:
## Review Summary

**Verdict: Approved** — the fix is correct, minimal, and well-targeted.

### Bug Analysis
When an admin token (`token_teams=None`) requests a listing endpoint (e.g. `GET /tools`), results are cached. A subsequent request with a visibility filter (`GET /tools?visibility=team`) previously hit the **same cache key** because `visibility` was not part of the hash. The cache hit returns directly (bypassing the query-level `WHERE visibility = ...` filter), so all tools were returned instead of only team-visibility tools.

### Fix Verification
- `visibility` is now included in `cache.hash_filters()` across all 6 service list operations (tool, a2a, prompt, resource, server, gateway)
- `hash_filters` accepts `**kwargs`, so no signature changes were needed
- Different visibility values produce distinct cache hashes — verified with direct `RegistryCache` tests
- Query-level visibility filter (`if visibility: query.where(...)`) provides defense-in-depth on cache miss

### Consistency
- 4 services (tool, a2a, prompt, resource) cache admin results — the bug manifested here
- 2 services (server, gateway) only cache public-only results — fix applied for consistency

### Changes Made During Review
- Rebased onto current `main` (clean linear history, no merge commits)
- Rewrote commit message to conventional commit format, preserving original author
- Added 5 unit tests for 100% differential coverage of the cache hash change:
  - Visibility parameter forwarded to `hash_filters` (with and without filter)
  - Distinct hashes for None/public/team/private using real `RegistryCache`
  - End-to-end cache key differentiation across two admin `list_tools` calls

All 5103 service unit tests pass.

commits.message:
fix(cache): include visibility in cache hash to prevent stale admin results

Admin tokens bypassed cache key differentiation for the visibility
filter, causing requests like /tools?visibility=team to return
unfiltered cached results. Add visibility to hash_filters() calls
across all six service list operations.

Signed-off-by: NAYANA.R <nayana.r7813@gmail.com>
Closes #3644
